source_refs.note: Topic 25.4.1 with its three For Information boxes (PDF 237-238). Population and resource figures are attributed to the book.

blocks.text: From the early 1700s changes in technology gave humans more control over their food supply, better defence against predators and remedies for many diseases, and made them less vulnerable to the climate. These changes let humans expand the carrying capacity of their habitats.

About 16% (1.28 billion) of the world's people live in developed countries and 84% (6.72 billion) in developing countries. According to the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, the 2023 census recorded Pakistan's population as 241.49 million, with an official growth rate of 2.55% a year.

items: Habitat destruction and changes in land use.
Depletion of natural resources such as freshwater and fossil fuels.
Greater chances of new epidemics and pandemics, starvation and malnutrition.

blocks.title: For information
blocks.text: The book notes that, according to the UN, Pakistan's population has now crossed 250 million, keeping it the fifth most populous country. Humans are only about 0.01% of the Earth's biomass; plants make up about 82% and bacteria about 13%. The wealthiest 20% of people consume 86% of the world's resources and produce 53% of its carbon dioxide emissions, while the poorest 20% consume only 1.3% and emit only 3%.

blocks.prompt: How did humans 'expand the carrying capacity' of their habitats?
blocks.explanation: Through technology: more control over food supply, defence against predators, medicines against disease and protection from the climate.

items: Technology since the 1700s raised human carrying capacity.
Pakistan: 241.49 million (2023 census), growth 2.55% a year.
Growth causes habitat loss, resource depletion, pollution and climate change.
